summary: Draft docs-first Session Manager Kernel DPC-threshold cluster record. `LongDpcQueueThreshold` and `LongDpcRuntimeThreshold` have explicit repo-doc defaults under `HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Session Manager\\Kernel`, both values are absent on the observed clean baseline, both produced exact current-build Unicode string hits in `ntoskrnl.exe`, and both survived a broad lightweight runtime replay that explicitly armed them from missing to `1` for one reboot while still returning `no-hit`. This keeps the family real and current-build-relevant, but still below the line for aggressive RE until a stronger caller, symbol, or live state clue appears.

setting.name: Kernel Long DPC Threshold Cluster
setting.casual_explanation: This cluster appears to expose low-level thresholds for what the kernel considers a long DPC queue condition and a long DPC runtime condition. It is kernel-adjacent and not a normal user setting.
setting.why_people_change_it: Kernel researchers may inspect these values when investigating DPC latency behavior, watchdog escalation, or undocumented scheduler-tuning guides.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: The cluster has explicit repo-doc defaults, clean baseline state, exact current-build string hits, and a broad runtime no-hit lane. It is strong enough for a schema-backed draft, but still too weak for a published tweak or a recommended non-default configuration.
setting.professional_notes: Repo docs list `LongDpcQueueThreshold = 3` and `LongDpcRuntimeThreshold = 100` under `Session Manager\\Kernel`, mapped to `KiLongDpcQueueThreshold` and `KiLongDpcRuntimeThreshold`. The kernel-power routing pass already grouped both values inside the `Session Manager\\Kernel` docs cluster. The observed clean baseline later confirmed that the parent key exists while both values are absent. The targeted current-build string batch then found exact Unicode hits for both values in `ntoskrnl.exe`, which is stronger than a pure docs-only lead and enough to keep the family out of raw backlog. The later lightweight runtime replay explicitly armed both values from `null` to `1`, rebooted once, and still left both values in the residual `no-hit` hold, which is more informative than a generic no-hit because it demonstrates that a simple present-and-nonzero mutation did not surface a trace hit in that broad lane. Existing source-enrichment outputs converge on the same low-priority next lane for both values: `timer-dpc-stress`, `windbg` queue. A follow-up repo scan first identified `Invoke-TimerResolutionTrigger` as the nearest reusable primitive, the guest mega-trigger runtime script then gained a dedicated `timer_dpc_stress` harness that layers `NtSetTimerResolution`, `timeBeginPeriod`, concurrent short-period `System.Threading.Timer` instances, and bounded CPU burst jobs, and the generic Procmon guest tool now exposes the same lane as `TriggerProfile = timer-dpc-stress`. That means the trigger-design gap is closed at both the guest harness and replay-wrapper layers: the next proof step is no longer harness invention, but replaying the cluster under the dedicated trigger and capturing whether any current-build query/read path appears. This cluster therefore belongs in the canonical research set, but as a docs-first DPC sibling family rather than an actively promoted tweak lane.

evidence.title: Repo system docs assign LongDpcQueueThreshold = 3 and LongDpcRuntimeThreshold = 100
evidence.summary: Repo docs list both values under `HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Session Manager\\Kernel` and map them to `KiLongDpcQueueThreshold` and `KiLongDpcRuntimeThreshold`.

evidence.title: Observed baseline existence for LongDpcQueueThreshold and LongDpcRuntimeThreshold
evidence.summary: The observed clean baseline confirmed that `HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Session Manager\\Kernel` exists while both `LongDpcQueueThreshold` and `LongDpcRuntimeThreshold` are absent.

evidence.title: Current-build string hits for LongDpcQueueThreshold and LongDpcRuntimeThreshold
evidence.summary: The broad current-build string batch found exact Unicode hits for both value names in `C:\\Windows\\System32\\ntoskrnl.exe`, with no supporting hits in the adjacent `smss.exe`, `winload.exe`, or `ci.dll` probes.

evidence.title: Lightweight runtime batch kept both LongDpc thresholds in residual no-hit hold
evidence.summary: The tools-hardened lightweight runtime lane explicitly armed both values from missing to `1`, rebooted once, and still kept both `system.kernel.long-dpc-queue-threshold` and `system.kernel.long-dpc-runtime-threshold` in the residual `no-hit` hold.

evidence.title: Source-enrichment keeps both LongDpc thresholds as docs-first new candidates
evidence.summary: Source-enrichment assigns both values the same low-support docs-first route bucket and converges on the same suggested next runtime family: `timer-dpc-stress`, low priority, `windbg` queue.

evidence.title: Repo guest tooling now exposes a dedicated timer-dpc-stress harness
evidence.summary: The guest mega-trigger runtime script now exposes `timer_dpc_stress`, and the generic Procmon guest tool now exposes `TriggerProfile = timer-dpc-stress`; both align directly with the enrichment recommendation for `timer-dpc-stress` triggers by combining timer-resolution changes, concurrent timers, and DPC-heavy workload.

decision.why: The cluster is strong enough for a canonical draft because it has explicit repo-doc defaults, observed baseline state, exact current-build string hits, and a real runtime replay that explicitly armed both values from missing to `1` while still leaving them in no-hit hold. It is not ready for validation because there is still no current-build caller, live value state, or primary Microsoft source for either value.

open_questions: Which current-build caller, if any, seeds or reads `KiLongDpcQueueThreshold` and `KiLongDpcRuntimeThreshold` from `Session Manager\\Kernel`?
Are the repo-doc defaults built-in live defaults, boot-only overrides, or stale mappings from an older build family?
Would a targeted `timer-dpc-stress` or debugger-assisted lane surface live state or a real query/set path for either value?
Does the new dedicated `timer_dpc_stress` harness surface a current-build query or read path for either value, or does the lane stay broad no-hit even under a narrower trigger?
